fields.description:
## Problem
Findings carry a `severity` string (`severity_label(impact)` -> critical/major/minor/none,
`review_kernel/decide.py`) that is derived from IMPACT ALONE, so it does not order the same way as
the authoritative `priority = validity x impact`. A high-impact/low-validity finding shows as
`critical` while ranking below a `major`. This is a foot-gun: it invites reading the label as the
gate signal when it is not. It also caused a field misread - via `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY`
(major->high, minor->medium, none->info) the review-bot surfaced the same finding as INFO then
MEDIUM across identical runs, reading like a severity change when only impact drifted.

## Idea
Make findings blocking / not-blocking + numeric priority, mirroring the intent that priority is
the single source of truth. Remove or rename the impact-only severity label so nothing mistakes it
for the decision.

## Corrected scope (post-decomposition research)
The review-kernel (`pass3_decide`) stops STAMPING `severity` onto its own emitted findings, and
every consumer of THOSE findings (aggregation/dedup where live, the Gerrit review-bot comment,
the CLI renderers, the workflow gate) is migrated to `priority`/`decision` instead. This does
NOT mean severity disappears everywhere: `findings.py`'s shared `SEVERITIES`/`normalize_finding`
vocabulary remains intact and untouched, because it also serves an entirely separate
completion-verification module cluster (`completion_reconcile.py`, `completion_child_gate.py`,
`epic_bug_screen.py`, `workflow/gate_ops.py`, `workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py`) and
the `spec_scan.py` "spec-alignment" reviewer -- neither of which ever computes `priority`/
`validity`/`impact`/`decision` and neither of which has anything to do with the impact-only
severity_label bug this epic is fixing. Two research-driven corrections during decomposition:
`aggregate.py::aggregate_findings` (originally named as a consumer) is confirmed dead code (no
caller since ADR 0075) and needs no change; `workflow/steps.py`'s `gate`/`fail_on_severity` is
not wired into any real production gate workflow (only a demo/sample and a test fixture use it)
so its migration is additive (a new `priority_threshold` alongside `fail_on_severity`, not a
replacement).

## Decomposition (each child independently reviewable, linear depends_on stack)
1. `pudgy-jolly-guppy` - ADR recording the decision (certified, closed, landed).
2. `uncheering-uncivil-pig` - assign fixed priority to DET-tier findings (secrets detector,
   bugfix-size gate) (closed, landed).
3. `beaming-snively-urial` - thread priority/decision through shim.py's `_to_common_finding`
   for the `review_result`/`review_code()` consumer (closed, landed). (`aggregate.py` and
   `spec_scan.py` are explicitly untouched -- see Corrected scope above.)
4. `patriotic-abdicative-arrowana` - fix `adapter.py::_translate_findings` to carry a
   `blocking: bool` (replacing a `severity` value nothing ever rendered), and update the CLI
   renderers that read `priority`/`decision`-bearing findings to show blocking/advisory
   instead of severity where such findings exist.
5. `camlet-exodermal-kodiakbear` - add a `priority_threshold` option to the (non-production,
   demo-only) `fail_on_severity` workflow gate policy, additive alongside the existing
   severity check.
6. `byzantine-spinelike-penguin` - stop the review-kernel from stamping `severity`; relax
   (not remove) the `severity` requirement on `review_result`'s schema-shared finding def
   (`completion_verdict`'s findings never come from the review-kernel, so its `severity` stays
   always-required and unaffected); remove the vestigial `BLOCKING_SEVERITIES` config and the
   duplicated `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY`/`_SEVERITY_DEFAULT` machinery in `shim.py`; amend
   ADR 0108 to record this corrected, narrower scope.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All child tickets are closed, each behind its own `Verified +1` / `LLM-Review +1`
  Gerrit change (`git log --grep "rebar-ticket: <child-id>"` finds a landed commit per child).
- [x] No finding produced by the review-kernel (`pass3_decide`, code-review or plan-review)
  carries a `severity` key once ticket 6 lands (`grep -rn '"severity"' src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`
  finds no finding-shape references outside historical comments/docstrings). Findings from
  OTHER producers (completion-verification cluster, `spec_scan.py`) continue to carry
  `severity` unchanged -- this is intentional, not a residual gap.
- [x] Every review-kernel-produced finding (LLM-scored and DET-tier) carries a `priority`
  float and a `decision` (`block`/`advisory`) key, and both the Gerrit comment and the CLI
  renderers for review-kernel-sourced findings show only blocking/advisory tags, never a
  severity word.
- [x] `make test` passes on the final stacked change (byzantine-spinelike-penguin).
- [x] The one documented compatibility note (severity no longer guaranteed present on
  review-kernel-sourced `review_result` findings) is present in `docs/release-notes.md` and
  `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Provenance
Discovered from the upstream review-code false-positive report (client project). Sibling of the
merge-base diff fix (ticket 8559-44c3-e08a-4bb9). Discovered work: ticket `broken-spirited-dorado`
(spec_scan.py priority migration) was created then obsoleted once the corrected scope above was
established -- see its ticket record for the reasoning.
